enonce_markdown: A programmer begins with the single task "Manage a school canteen", splits it into "record meals", "collect payments" and "print reports", and then splits each of these into smaller tasks until each can be coded easily. Which design approach is being used?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Top-down design starts with the whole problem and refines it step by step into smaller sub-problems. Bottom-up design starts from small existing components and assembles them.

### Solution

Starting with the overall task and breaking it down into smaller and smaller subtasks (stepwise refinement) is **top-down design**. Bottom-up design would begin with low-level routines and combine them. Prototyping builds a working trial version, and random design is not a recognised approach.

enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a main advantage of dividing a large program into modules?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Modular design breaks a system into separate parts with defined interfaces, so that parts can be written, tested and changed on their own.

### Solution

Because each module has a clear job and an interface, different programmers can develop and test modules separately, and a faulty module can be corrected or replaced without rewriting the whole program. The other statements are false: modular programs are not automatically faster, they still need testing (including integration testing), and they still need documentation.

choix.texte: Modules can be developed, tested and maintained separately by different programmers.
The program always runs faster than a single block of code.
No testing is needed once each module has been written.

enonce_markdown: Which of the following lists the stages of the software development life cycle in the correct order?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The life cycle moves from understanding the problem (analysis), to planning the solution (design), to building it (coding), to checking it (testing), and finally to keeping it working (maintenance).

### Solution

The logical order is analysis, design, coding, testing, maintenance. The other orders place coding before the problem is understood or maintenance before testing, which is not possible, because maintenance applies to a system that has already been delivered.

enonce_markdown: A single module of a payroll program calculates tax, prints payslips and also updates the bank file. Programmers find it very difficult to change one of these tasks without breaking another. Which design weakness does this describe?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Good modules have high cohesion (each does one well-defined job) and low coupling (little dependence on other modules).

### Solution

A module that performs three unrelated jobs has **low cohesion**, and changing one job risks the others. The aim is one job per module. Option a is the opposite of the desired property. Normalisation concerns database tables, and information hiding is a principle to be applied, not a weakness.

enonce_markdown:
A secondary school in Bamenda wants a program to produce the end-of-term report cards of all its students.

(a) Use top-down design to break the task "Produce report cards" into at least three first-level modules, and break one of them into at least two further modules. Show the result as an indented list. (4 marks)

(b) For one module of your design, state its inputs and its output. (2 marks)

(c) Explain why the modules should have low coupling. (2 marks)
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Top-down design divides a task into subtasks, level by level, until each module has a single clear job. Each module is described by its inputs and outputs (its interface).

### Solution

**(a)** One acceptable decomposition:

```text
Produce report cards
  1. Read student data and marks
  2. Calculate results
       2.1 Calculate the average of each subject
       2.2 Calculate the overall average and the rank
  3. Print the report card of each student
```

**(b)** Module 2.2: inputs, the list of subject averages and the number of students; output, the overall average and the rank of each student.

**(c)** Low coupling means a module depends very little on the internals of the others, so it can be changed, tested or replaced without altering the other modules, and an error in one module is less likely to spread to the others.

enonce_markdown: A client in Buea needs an inventory system for her shops but cannot describe all the requirements in advance; she says she will know what she wants when she sees a working version. Which development approach is the most suitable?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Choose a model from the stability of the requirements. Stable and well-understood requirements suit a linear approach. Unclear or changing requirements need working versions shown to the client early and refined repeatedly.

### Solution

Since the client will only recognise her needs by seeing a working system, **iterative development with rapid prototyping** (build a prototype, obtain feedback, improve it, repeat) is best. A waterfall approach freezes the requirements before coding and would deliver a system the client may reject. A single delivery with no client contact would present the same risk, and coding immediately without any model leads to unstructured and unmaintainable software.

choix.texte: One delivery after all the coding, with no contact with the client until the end
Waterfall: fix all the requirements first and then follow each stage once
Iterative development with rapid prototyping and regular client feedback
No development model: start coding immediately
